1sfn92p: To form the imperfect subjunctive you do not need to memorise a new list: start from the third person plural of the preterite, drop «-ron» and add the endings. 4f098k: There are two sets of endings, in -ra and in -se, and they mean the same. The -ra form is the most frequent in conversation across Latin America and Spain; the -se form appears above all in writing and careful speech. The «nosotros» form always carries a written accent, because the word becomes stressed on the third-to-last syllable.

4yfyew: «Decir», «insistir en» and «escribir» either inform or request. If they inform, they take the indicative: «insistió en que el piso era de pinotea». If they request, the subjunctive: «insistió en que lo encerásemos cada mes». And if someone asked for something in the past but the request is still pending today, the present subjunctive is also possible: «me pidió que la llame el jueves» (Thursday has not come yet).

bv17ii: Original SpanishCue text written as a feature for the fictional magazine «Vecinos de San Telmo». The people and the café are invented.
10gov26: For sixty years, the corner of Defensa and Carlos Calvo kept a fixed schedule: at seven sharp, Delia Ferraro raised the shutter and switched on the lamps of Café Delia. When it closed two years ago, many of us thought the corner would become another souvenir shop. We were wrong. On Saturday, her grandchildren Martina and Joaquín reopened the premises, and they did it with a list of requests that Delia herself left them in writing.
1riw1p3: The list wasn't long, but it was precise. Delia asked them not to change the name, to keep the marble tables and for the waiters to keep calling customers by their names. She also wanted the menu always to include a cheap dish, «so that nobody would be left out for lack of money». Martina says that at first this condition seemed impossible to her with today's prices: «I told my brother we needed to make money, and he reminded me that Grandma had never wanted to get rich from the café».
1vpkmld: Not everything was obedience. Joaquín admits they argued a lot about the music. Delia disliked bars playing songs at full volume, and she would not allow anyone to play the piano without her permission. The siblings decided the piano would be played only on Fridays, with a guest pianist, and that the rest of the week the noise would be the usual: cups, newspapers and conversation. «I don't know whether she would agree with everything», Joaquín admits, «but I think she would be glad that people were staying for hours again».
t5upwa: We at this magazine allow ourselves an opinion. A list of requests can become a cage if it is read to the letter, and Café Delia has avoided that. The grandchildren did not copy their grandmother: through her papers, they asked her what she wanted to survive. If only more businesses in the neighbourhood had that luck, or that patience. For now, the shutter goes up at seven again.
